title: Sample: starting before you feel ready

slides.headline: You do not need to feel **ready** to start
slides.sub: Swipe for what to do instead

slides.headline: Ready is a feeling, and feelings show up late
slides.body: Most people wait for confidence before they begin. Confidence usually shows up after the first few messy tries.

slides.headline: Pick the smallest version
slides.body: Not the whole plan. One post, one page, one call. Small enough that you cannot talk yourself out of it.

slides.headline: Three small starts
items: Tell one person what you are building
Set a 20 minute timer and stop when it rings

slides.text: A rough start beats a perfect plan that never leaves your notes app.

slides.headline: Let it be a draft
slides.body: Drafts are allowed to be bad. You are collecting proof that you can move.

slides.headline: Start the small version today
slides.body: Tell me which one you picked.

caption:
Waiting to feel ready is one of the quietest ways to stay stuck.

Pick the smallest version of the thing and do it today. Rough is fine.

Tell me in the comments which small start you picked.

Comment START and I will cheer you on.
